title: How to spot a fake natty: rollercoaster progress
summary: First episode of a series on recognising fake naturals without naming anyone. NH's first sign is rollercoaster progress: naturals keep most of what they build and regain it quickly via muscle memory, whereas steroid users balloon in size and strength for a few months, disappear, and return much smaller, often low in energy. He urges viewers to stay natural.

claims.claim: NH won't make the channel a call-out channel and will never name anyone; his signs come from long experience around gyms.
For naturals, muscle gained is hard to lose: legs built to 25 inches will shrink during a long layoff but won't drop back to 20 inches.
When naturals return to training, muscle memory makes lost size come back very fast.
PEDs put the body in a hormonal surplus; when users stop, the hormones disappear and the body can't sustain the size, so it shrinks back toward square one.
A sign of a fake natty: a gym regular suddenly gains lots of size and strength out of nowhere for 1-3 months, disappears, and returns about a month later much smaller.
People coming off cycles often seem to have less energy, less aggression and look confused.
The idea that you keep your size after stopping steroids is false; you lose most of your gains.
Because the gains vanish when they stop, many users become dependent and stay on for life.
Steroids are physically traumatic but the mental toll is worse: losing the gains can cause depression, especially in people passionate about the gym.
Natural progress is a very slow slope with no peaks and crashes, but it never regresses and stays with you for life.
